mainTopic: The forgotten הלכות after משה's death and how עתניאל restored them; the five חטאות מתות apply only to an individual, not the ציבור
overview: The גמרא first finishes explaining the 'דופי' (flaw) that began after יוסף בן יועזר: it was the first מחלוקת, the dispute about סמיכה, and he argued about it only when old age had weakened him. It then returns to שמואל's teaching that 3,000 הלכות were forgotten while the people mourned משה. Leader after leader refused to recover them through prophecy, because the Torah is 'not in heaven' and a נביא may not add anything new. One of the forgotten laws was the law of a חטאת whose owner died. רבי אבהו says עתניאל בן קנז restored the lost teachings through his sharp reasoning. This leads to stories about עכסה, about כלב's family, and about עתניאל, who is also called יעבץ. רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא give two readings of יעבץ's prayer: one about Torah, one mostly about worldly blessings. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה. רבי שמעון teaches that all five חטאות מתות apply only to an individual's offering and never to a communal one, learning the two unclear cases from the three clear ones.

steps.title: The 'flaw' means the dispute over placing hands
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the 'דופי' mentioned in the ברייתא means the first disagreement among the sages, the dispute about סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The ברייתא is talking about the 'flaw' of the dispute over placing hands (סמיכה).
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers a difficulty from the previous discussion. He says the 'flaw' that began after יוסף בן יועזר was not a sin. It was the start of מחלוקת in Torah, beginning with the argument over סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that until יוסף בן יועזר died there was no 'דופי' among the sages. One might think this means no sage ever sinned, which is hard to accept. רב יוסף redefines the word: 'דופי' means that the sages were no longer fully united in their Torah, and the first open dispute was about placing hands on a קרבן on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning or placing one's hands on the head of a קרבן before it is slaughtered

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is teaching about the flaw of placing hands.
phrases.notes: This is the famous first מחלוקת: whether you may lean on a קרבן on יום טוב. It's discussed in חגיגה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty from the earlier part of the daf about what 'דופי' in the ברייתא means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word: 'flaw' means the dispute over סמיכה, not a sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'דופי' could have meant a moral flaw or sin among the sages.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'דופי' means the beginning of disagreement in Torah law, starting with סמיכה.

steps.title: But יוסף בן יועזר himself argued about placing hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: יוסף בן יועזר was himself one of the first two sages to argue about סמיכה, so the dispute already existed in his lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: But יוסף בן יועזר himself argued about סמיכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's answer. If the 'flaw' is the סמיכה dispute, that dispute already started while יוסף בן יועזר was alive, because he was part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the flaw began only after יוסף בן יועזר died. Yet the first pair to argue about סמיכה was יוסף בן יועזר and יוסף בן יוחנן. So the 'flaw' existed in his own lifetime, which seems to contradict the ברייתא as רב יוסף explained it.

keyTerms.meaning: He actually disagreed (a doubled verb for emphasis)

phrases.english: But Yosef ben Yo'ezer himself
actually disagreed about placing hands!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר גּוּפֵיהּ מִיפְלָיג פְּלִיג בִּסְמִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's explanation from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the 'flaw' refers to the סמיכה dispute.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סמיכה dispute involved יוסף בן יועזר himself, so it began during his lifetime, not after his death as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: He argued only in his old age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that יוסף בן יועזר argued about סמיכה only at the end of his life, when his mind was weakened by age.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he argued about it, it was at the end of his years, when his heart (understanding) had become limited.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף. The dispute did happen in יוסף בן יועזר's lifetime, but only in his last years, when old age had weakened his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His full Torah clarity is measured by his years of strength. Once age weakened his understanding, it is as if his era of complete Torah had already ended. So the dispute counts as coming after his time, and the ברייתא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of his years

phrases.english: When he disagreed about it, it was at the end of his years,
when the heart had become limited.
phrases.notes: 'Heart' here means his mind and understanding, weakened by old age.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִיפְּלִיג בַּהּ בְּסוֹף שְׁנֵיהּ דִּבְצַר לִיבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the time frame: the dispute came only in his weakened old age.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he argued during his life, the flaw existed before his death.
steps.terutzMaskana: His argument came when his understanding was weakened, so it counts as after his era of full Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'flaw' after יוסף בן יועזר is the start of מחלוקת (the סמיכה dispute). He himself argued only in old age, so the ברייתא still holds.

steps.title: Three thousand laws forgotten while mourning משה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's statement that 3,000 הלכות were forgotten during the mourning for משה. יהושע refused to ask Heaven for them, because the Torah is 'not in heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main statement: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Three thousand הלכות were forgotten in the days of mourning for משה. The people said to יהושע, 'Ask (Heaven)!' He said to them, 'It is not in heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'גופא' tells us the גמרא is now looking closely at a statement it quoted earlier. שמואל teaches that many laws were lost when משה died, and יהושע would not recover them through prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people wanted יהושע, a נביא, to get the lost laws straight from Heaven. He refused, quoting 'לא בשמים היא.' Once the Torah was given at סיני, deciding הלכה belongs to the sages using their reasoning, not to prophecy.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself; the גמרא now analyzes a statement quoted earlier
The days of mourning for him
'It is not in heaven': Torah law is decided by the sages, not by heavenly messages

steps.whyThisMatters: 'לא בשמים היא' is a basic rule across ש״ס: הלכה is decided by the sages' reasoning, and a prophet cannot settle it by prophecy.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Three thousand halachot were forgotten
in the days of mourning for Moshe.
They said to Yehoshua: Ask!
phrases.notes: He means: ask ה׳ through prophecy to tell you the lost laws.

phrases.english: He said to them: "It is not in heaven."
phrases.notes: דברים 30:12

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the סמיכה discussion back to an earlier statement of שמואל, to analyze it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lost הלכות cannot be recovered through prophecy, because the Torah is 'not in heaven.'

steps.title: שמואל the prophet also refuses to ask
steps.stepSummary: Generations later the people asked שמואל הנביא to get the laws from Heaven. He refused, learning from 'אלה המצות' that a prophet may not add anything new to the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to שמואל (the prophet), 'Ask!' He said to them, 'These are the commandments,' meaning that from now on a prophet is not allowed to introduce anything new.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues to a later generation. שמואל הנביא gives the same refusal as יהושע, but he brings a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלה' (these) limits the מצוות to the ones given through משה. From then on, a נביא has no power to add or change Torah law through prophecy. This backs up יהושע's answer with a second source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These are the commandments': only these, the ones given to משה

steps.confusionAlert: This שמואל is שמואל הנביא from נביאים, not the אמורא שמואל who reported this whole teaching in Step 4.

phrases.english: They said to Shmuel: Ask!
He said to them: "These are the commandments" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:34

phrases.english: meaning that a prophet is not permitted
to introduce anything new from now on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's teaching: a second prophet, in a later generation, refuses in the same way, using a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נביא may not introduce new Torah law; 'אלה המצות' closes the מצוות after משה.

steps.title: The law of a sin offering whose owner died was also forgotten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא adds that the law of a חטאת whose owner died was one of the laws forgotten during the mourning for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: The law of a חטאת whose owners died was also forgotten in the days of mourning for משה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא ties the story of the forgotten laws back to our topic. One of the forgotten laws was what to do with a חטאת whose owner died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (also) adds a specific example to שמואל's 3,000 forgotten laws. Our פרק deals with the חטאות that are left to die, including a חטאת whose owner died. This sets up the next step, where the people ask פנחס and אלעזר to recover this law from Heaven, and both refuse.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:
Also, the law of a sin offering whose owners died
was forgotten in the days of mourning for Moshe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא: אַף חַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a specific example, connected to our פרק, to שמואל's list of forgotten laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of a חטאת whose owner died was among the הלכות forgotten when משה died.
steps.whatToRemember: 3,000 הלכות were forgotten when משה died, and prophecy cannot bring them back ('לא בשמים היא'; 'אלה המצות'). The law of a חטאת whose owner died was one of them.

steps.title: פנחס and אלעזר refuse to ask Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The people ask פנחס, then אלעזר, to get a forgotten law from Heaven. Both refuse. פנחס says the Torah is 'not in heaven.' אלעזר says that after 'אלה המצות' no נביא may add anything new.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to פנחס: Ask Heaven! He said: 'It is not in heaven.' They said to אלעזר: Ask! He said: 'These are the commandments.' This means that from now on a prophet may not bring anything new.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story about a forgotten law. Two great leaders are asked to get the answer from Heaven, and both say no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the two reasons we already saw in steps 4 and 5. פנחס uses יהושע's reason, that the Torah is 'not in heaven.' אלעזר uses שמואל הנביא's reason, that a נביא may not make anything new. So both ideas go back to the very first leaders after משה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not in heaven.' The Torah was given to people, and it is decided here on earth.
To bring something new into the Torah's laws

phrases.english: They said to Pinchas: Ask!
He said to them: "It is not in heaven."
phrases.notes: דברים 30:12

phrases.english: They said to Elazar: Ask!
He said to them: "These are the commandments,"
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק that שמואל הנביא used in step 5.

phrases.english: which teaches that a prophet is not allowed
to bring anything new from now on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of the forgotten law of a חטאת whose owner died. The leaders refuse to get it back from Heaven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forgotten law may not be brought back through prophecy. The Torah is not in heaven, and a נביא may not add anything new.

steps.title: יהושע loses 300 laws when משה dies
steps.stepSummary: רב says that before משה died, he told יהושע to ask about anything he was unsure of. יהושע said he had never left משה's side, so he had no questions. Right away he forgot 300 הלכות, 700 new doubts came up, and the people rose up to kill him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When משה was about to leave for גן עדן, he told יהושע: Ask me about every doubt you have. יהושע said: רבי, did I ever leave you for even one moment? Didn't you write about me that יהושע 'did not leave the tent'? Right away יהושע grew weak. He forgot 300 laws, 700 doubts came up, and all of ישראל stood up to kill him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story from רב about how יהושע forgot laws at the very moment משה was leaving the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע felt sure he had no questions, because he had always stayed with משה. That very moment he lost 300 הלכות and was left with 700 new doubts. This adds to step 4: it shows how the forgetting came about, and why the people were so angry.

keyTerms.meaning: The Garden of Eden, where משה went when he died
Doubts, cases where the law is unclear

steps.confusionAlert: In step 4 שמואל said 3,000 laws were forgotten. Here רב says יהושע forgot 300. These are separate statements with different numbers. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנִּפְטַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לְגַן עֵדֶן,
phrases.english: At the time when Moshe our teacher was leaving for the Garden of Eden,
he said to Yehoshua:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאַל מִמֶּנִּי כָּל סְפֵיקוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָךְ.
phrases.english: Ask me about all the doubts that you have.
He said to him: My teacher,
did I ever leave you for even one moment
and go somewhere else?
Didn't you write this about me:
"And his attendant, Yehoshua son of Nun, a young man,
phrases.notes: שמות 33:11

phrases.english: did not leave the tent"?
phrases.notes: He means: I was always with you, so I would already have asked about anything I didn't know.

phrases.english: Right away, Yehoshua's strength grew weak,
and he forgot three hundred laws,
and seven hundred doubts came up for him,
and all of Israel rose up to kill him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנִּפְטַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לְגַן עֵדֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that tells more about how laws were forgotten when משה died, this time from יהושע's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When משה died, יהושע forgot 300 laws and was left with 700 doubts, and the people turned against him.

steps.title: God sends יהושע to war instead of restoring the laws
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells יהושע He cannot tell him the forgotten laws. Instead, יהושע should keep the people busy with war. The proof is the פסוק saying that right after משה died, ה׳ spoke to יהושע and told him to cross the ירדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to him: It is impossible to tell you. Go and keep them busy with war, as it says: 'And it was after the death of משה, servant of ה׳, that ה׳ said...'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. God answers יהושע's crisis and backs it up with a פסוק from the start of ספר יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even God will not give back the forgotten laws, because the Torah is 'not in heaven.' The answer to the people's anger is not new prophecy. It is to keep them busy with the war. The פסוק shows God spoke to יהושע about the conquest right after משה died.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)

steps.whatToRemember: Even right after משה died, a forgotten law could not be brought back from Heaven. The Torah is in human hands now.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
To tell you is impossible,
phrases.notes: That is, I can't tell you the forgotten laws, because the Torah is 'not in heaven' (step 4).

phrases.english: go and keep them busy with war,
as it says: "And it was after the death of Moshe,
phrases.notes: יהושע 1:1. The next פסוק goes on to tell יהושע to cross the ירדן.

phrases.english: servant of ה׳, that ה׳ said, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: לוֹמַר לָךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's story: God's answer to יהושע's crisis, backed by a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God would not give back the forgotten laws. He told יהושע to keep the people busy with war instead.

steps.title: 1,700 teachings forgotten while mourning משה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 1,700 קל וחומר teachings, גזירות שוות, and fine points of the סופרים were forgotten during the days of mourning for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: One thousand seven hundred קל וחומר teachings, גזירות שוות, and fine points of the סופרים were forgotten during the days of mourning for משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds another list of what was forgotten when משה died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we heard about forgotten laws. This ברייתא adds that the methods of learning were also lost: hundreds of קל וחומר teachings, גזירות שוות, and careful details of the סופרים. The loss included the reasoning behind the laws, not just the laws themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if a rule holds in a lighter case, it surely holds in a stricter one
Learning a law by comparing the same word used in two places in the Torah
Fine points and careful details taught by the early sages

steps.confusionAlert: Here בְּמַתְנִיתִין does not mean our משנה. In this line it means a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
One thousand seven hundred kal vachomer teachings,
and gezeirah shavah teachings,
and fine points of the scribes
were forgotten during the days of mourning for Moshe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about another kind of forgotten Torah: the methods of learning, not only the laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the mourning for משה, 1,700 קל וחומר teachings, גזירות שוות, and fine points of the סופרים were forgotten.

steps.title: עתניאל brought back the forgotten laws
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says that even though the laws were forgotten, עתניאל בן קנז restored them through his sharp reasoning, and he brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: Even so, עתניאל בן קנז brought them back through his sharp thinking, as the פסוק says: 'And עתניאל בן קנז, the brother of כלב, captured it, and he gave him עכסה his daughter as a wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: After all the stories about laws being lost, רבי אבהו gives a hopeful ending: עתניאל won them back with his sharp mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said 1,700 teachings were forgotten. רבי אבהו says they were not lost forever, because עתניאל rebuilt them by reasoning them out. The proof is the פסוק about capturing a city, which is read as capturing Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp, careful reasoning in Torah learning

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that Torah lost through forgetting can be rebuilt through deep reasoning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
Even so, he restored them,
Othniel son of Kenaz, through his sharp reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּלְכְּדָהּ עׇתְנִיאֵל בֶּן קְנַז אֲחִי כָלֵב
phrases.english: as it is stated: "And Othniel son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, captured it,
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:17. The city he captured was קרית ספר, "the city of the book," so capturing it hints at winning back Torah.

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּתֶּן לוֹ אֶת עַכְסָה בִתּוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״.
phrases.english: and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֶחְזִירָן עׇתְנִיאֵל בֶּן קְנַז מִתּוֹךְ פִּלְפּוּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the loss described in step 10 by saying the laws were restored.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עתניאל בן קנז restored the forgotten laws through his sharp reasoning.

steps.title: Why she was called עכסה
steps.stepSummary: The name עכסה is explained as a play on כעס: anyone who saw her became angry at his own wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was she called עכסה? Because anyone who saw her became angry at his own wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the name of עכסה, the daughter of כלב who married עתניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of עכסה are close to כעס, "anger." She was so beautiful that men who saw her got upset that their own wives were not like her.

phrases.english: And why was she called "Achsah"?
Because anyone who saw her
became angry at his own wife.
phrases.notes: A play on the name: עכס sounds like כעס, "anger."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on עכסה, who is named in the פסוק of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name עכסה hints at כעס, because her beauty made men angry at their own wives.

steps.title: What does ותצנח mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק about עכסה and asks what the word ותצנח means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And when she came, she urged him to ask her father for a field, and she ותצנח from on the donkey.' What does ותצנח mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק about עכסה and asks about one unusual word in it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply, ותצנח means she got down from the donkey. The גמרא feels the word hints at more, and asks what is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: And she got down; the גמרא also reads it as crying out

phrases.english: "And it came to pass when she came, that she urged him
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:18.

phrases.english: to ask her father for a field,
and she got down from the donkey."
What is meant by "vatitznach"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק about עכסה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The deeper meaning of the word ותצנח.

steps.title: Like a hungry donkey, she cried out
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רבי יצחק explains that עכסה compared herself to a donkey that cries out when it has no food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says in the name of רבי יצחק: She said to him: Just as this donkey cries out right away when there is no food in its trough, so a woman cries out right away when there is no grain in her house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: ותצנח means she cried out, using the donkey as a picture of her complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of just getting off the donkey, עכסה used it as an example. A hungry donkey brays at once; a woman with no food at home complains at once. She was telling her father she needed support.

phrases.english: Rava says that Rabbi Yitzchak says:
She said to him: Just as this donkey,
phrases.notes: "Him" is her father, כלב.

phrases.english: once it has no food in its trough,
immediately cries out,
so too a woman, once she has no
grain in her house,
immediately cries out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמְרָה לוֹ מָה חֲמוֹר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ותצנח means she cried out, comparing herself to a hungry donkey that brays.

steps.title: A home dry of all good, a husband with only Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains עכסה's request: the נגב hints at a home empty of goods, and 'springs of water' hints at a husband who has only Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she said: Give me a blessing, for you have given me the land of the נגב' — a house dried out of all good things. 'And give me springs of water' — a man who has nothing but Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next פסוק as עכסה's complaint about her poor home and her husband who only learns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נגב sounds like מנוגב, "dried out," so she means her house has nothing in it. Water is a picture of Torah, so 'springs of water' means her husband has Torah but no money to feed her.

phrases.english: "And she said: Give me a blessing,
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:19.

phrases.english: for you have given me the land of the Negev";
a house that is dried out of all good things.
phrases.notes: A play on words: נגב sounds like מנוגב, "dried out."

phrases.english: "And give me springs of water":

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: a man who has nothing in him but Torah alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with the next פסוק, spelling out her complaint.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עכסה complains that her home is empty and her husband has only Torah.

steps.title: כלב answers: a Torah scholar needs no one to ask for him
steps.stepSummary: כלב gives her the upper and lower springs, which the גמרא reads as his reply: someone who lives in the upper and lower worlds does not need food requested for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And כלב gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.' He said to her: Someone who lives among the upper ones and the lower ones — should food be requested for him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the end of the פסוק as כלב's answer to his daughter's complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עכסה worried that a man of Torah cannot support her. כלב answers that a Torah scholar is connected to both heaven and earth, so he will surely be taken care of; no one needs to beg food for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper and lower worlds (heaven and earth)

steps.whatToRemember: The story of עכסה teaches that a person who learns Torah is cared for from Above, even if he looks poor.

phrases.english: "And Caleb gave her the upper springs
and the lower springs":

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהּ: מִי שֶׁדָּר עֶלְיוֹנִים וְתַחְתּוֹנִים
phrases.english: He said to her: One who dwells among the upper and the lower worlds,
should food be requested for him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁדָּר עֶלְיוֹנִים וְתַחְתּוֹנִים יְבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ מְזוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives כלב's reply to the complaint in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah scholar, connected to heaven and earth, does not need others to ask food for him.

steps.title: Was כלב really the son of קנז?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how כלב can be called the son of קנז, when the פסוק calls him כלב בן יפונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And was כלב the son of קנז? Isn't he 'כלב בן יפונה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a contradiction about who כלב's father was and raises it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק called עתניאל בן קנז 'the brother of כלב,' which suggests כלב was also a son of קנז. But elsewhere he is called כלב בן יפונה, so which was his father?

keyTerms.meaning: Caleb son of Jephunneh, his usual name

phrases.english: And was Caleb the son of Kenaz?
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in step 11, which calls עתניאל בן קנז "the brother of כלב."

phrases.english: But isn't he "Caleb son of Jephunneh"!
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:13.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָלֵב בֶּן קְנַז הוּא וַהֲלֹא כָּלֵב בֶּן יְפוּנֶּה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the wording of the פסוק in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication in the פסוק that כלב was a son of קנז.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק names his father as יפונה, so he cannot be the son of קנז.

steps.title: יפונה means he turned away from the spies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that יפונה is not his father's name but a description: he turned away from the plan of the spies.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'יפונה' mean? That he turned away from the plan of the spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction: יפונה is not a father's name at all. It is a nickname that praises כלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יפונה comes from the root פנה, "to turn." כלב turned away from the spies who spoke badly about ארץ ישראל. So 'בן יפונה' describes what he did and does not name a father, and calling him בן קנז no longer clashes with it. Step 20 will explain exactly how he was connected to קנז.
steps.whatToRemember: The name יפונה is a description, not a father's name. It praises כלב for turning away from the spies.

phrases.english: What is meant by "Jephunneh"?
That he turned away from the plan of the spies.
phrases.notes: A play on words: יפונה sounds like פנה, "turned."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a name as a description
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יפונה was the name of כלב's father, which would contradict 'son of קנז.'
steps.terutzMaskana: יפונה is not a father's name. It describes how he turned away from the spies, so it does not clash with 'בן קנז'.

steps.title: But wasn't כלב the son of חצרון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises another problem with calling כלב the son of קנז: a פסוק calls him the son of חצרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, was he really the son of קנז? He was the son of חצרון, as the פסוק says: 'And כלב son of חצרון had children with עזובה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the idea that כלב was the son of קנז, using a פסוק that names a different father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the גמרא explained that יפונה is a description and not a real name. Even so, there is still a problem, because דברי הימים openly calls כלב the son of חצרון. So how can anyone call him the son of קנז?

keyTerms.meaning: But still. Used when a problem remains even after an earlier answer.
חצרון, named in דברי הימים as כלב's father.

phrases.english: But still, was he the son of Kenaz?
He was the son of Hezron,
as it is written: "And Caleb son of Hezron
had children with Azubah."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up challenge that remains after step 18's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that כלב was the son of קנז.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in דברי הימים names חצרון as כלב's father, which seems to contradict calling him בן קנז.

steps.title: כלב was the stepson of קנז
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that כלב was the real son of חצרון and the stepson of קנז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He was קנז's stepson.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by saying that both names are correct. חצרון was כלב's real father, and קנז was his stepfather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים are not really in conflict. 'Son of חצרון' describes his birth father. 'Son of קנז' describes the family he was raised in, since a stepson can be called by his stepfather's name.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He was the stepson of Kenaz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonizing the two פסוקים: one names the birth father, the other names the stepfather.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give כלב two different fathers.
steps.terutzMaskana: כלב was born to חצרון and raised as the stepson of קנז.
steps.whatToRemember: כלב had three titles: בן יפונה is a description (he turned away from the spies), בן חצרון names his real father, and בן קנז names his stepfather.

steps.title: עתניאל and יעבץ are one person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that עתניאל, יעבץ, and יהודה are all the same person, and explains the names עתניאל and יעבץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: The same man is עתניאל and is יעבץ. What is his real name? יהודה, the brother of שמעון. He is called עתניאל because God answered him, and יעבץ because he advised and spread Torah in Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא teaches that עתניאל and יעבץ are two names for one person, whose real name was יהודה, and it explains what each name means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is read as a short description. עתניאל is split into ענאו אל, 'God answered him.' יעבץ is read as יעץ ורבץ, 'advised and spread' Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: That God answered him. The meaning drawn from the name עתניאל.
He advised and spread (Torah). The meaning drawn from the name יעבץ.
עתניאל, the son of קנז and the first שופט.

phrases.english: A tanna taught:
He is Othniel, and he is Jabez,
And what is his real name?
Judah, brother of Simeon, is his name.
"Othniel": because God answered him,
"Jabez": because he advised and spread
Torah among Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having mentioned עתניאל as כלב's half-brother through קנז, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about עתניאל's names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עתניאל = יעבץ = יהודה. The names mean 'God answered him' and 'he advised and spread Torah.'

steps.title: Where do we see that God answered him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that God answered עתניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that God answered him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the first explanation of the name, that God answered him. This question sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explained the name עתניאל as 'God answered him.' The גמרא now wants a פסוק that shows him praying and being answered.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know? A request for a source.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that God answered him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the meaning of the name given in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that God answered עתניאל/יעבץ.

steps.title: יעבץ's prayer in דברי הימים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where יעבץ prays and God grants his request.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'And יעבץ called out to the God of Israel, saying: If You will truly bless me, and enlarge my border, and Your hand will be with me, and You will keep me from evil so it will not pain me. And God brought about what he asked.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that shows יעבץ praying, followed by the words 'God brought about what he asked.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last words of the פסוק, ויבא אלהים את אשר שאל, are the proof that God answered him. The detailed requests in the middle will be explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And God brought about what he asked. The proof that he was answered.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Jabez called
to the God of Israel, saying:
If You will truly bless me,
and enlarge my border,
and Your hand will be with me,
and keep me from evil, so that it will not pain me.
And God brought about what he asked."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 4:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ends by saying God granted what יעבץ asked.

steps.title: Each request is about Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads each phrase of יעבץ's prayer as a request connected to Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If You will truly bless me': in Torah. 'And enlarge my border': with students. 'And Your hand will be with me': that my learning will not be forgotten from my heart. 'And keep me from evil (מרעתי)': that I will find friends (ריעים) like me. 'So it will not pain me': that the יצר הרע will not overpower me and stop me from learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the prayer phrase by phrase and shows that every request was really about Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase that sounds like an ordinary request is read as a spiritual one: blessing means Torah, 'border' means students, and so on. The word מרעתי is read as if it came from רֵעַ, 'friend.' This fits the name יעבץ, the one who spread Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Friends, study companions. A wordplay on מֵרָעָתִי.
From learning, from reviewing my studies.

phrases.english: "If You will truly bless me": in Torah,
"And enlarge my border": with students,
"And Your hand will be with me":
that my learning will not be forgotten from my heart,
"And keep me from evil":
that friends like me will come my way,
phrases.notes: A play on words: מרעתי sounds like ריעים, 'friends.'

phrases.english: "So that it will not pain me":
that the evil inclination will not overpower me and keep me from learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each phrase of the פסוק quoted in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every request in יעבץ's prayer was about Torah: blessing in learning, students, remembering, good friends, and protection from the יצר הרע.

steps.title: God answered him right away
steps.stepSummary: יעבץ ends his prayer by saying that without these things he would go to the grave in sadness, and God answered him immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If You do this, good. And if not, I will go to the grave in my sadness.' Immediately, 'And God brought about what he asked.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the prayer and shows that God answered it right away. This closes the proof that God answered עתניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעבץ's plea shows how much Torah meant to him: without it, life would end in sadness. The ending of the פסוק, 'God brought about what he asked,' confirms the meaning of the name עתניאל, 'God answered him,' from step 21.
steps.whatToRemember: עתניאל, also called יעבץ, was named for being answered by God. His prayer, which was all about Torah, was granted right away.

phrases.english: If You do so, good,
and if not,
I will go in my sadness to the grave.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'in my sadness.'

phrases.english: Immediately, "And God brought about what he asked."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the prayer and returns to the end of the פסוק as the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: God answered יעבץ's prayer for Torah immediately, which proves the meaning of the name עתניאל, 'God answered him.'

steps.title: A teacher who teaches gains light, and one who refuses loses his wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן reads a פסוק in משלי about a student asking his teacher to teach him תורה. If the teacher teaches, both grow. If he refuses, God can take the teacher's wisdom and give it to the student.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, you can explain the פסוק: 'The poor man and the man in the middle meet; ה׳ lights up the eyes of both of them.' When a student goes to his teacher and asks him to teach him תורה, if the teacher teaches him, ה׳ lights up the eyes of both. If not, then 'the rich and the poor meet; ה׳ made them all': the One Who made this one wise can make him foolish, and the One Who made that one foolish can make him wise. This is the teaching of רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a similar lesson connected to the תורה theme of יעבץ's prayer. A פסוק in משלי teaches what happens when a student asks a teacher to teach him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'poor man' is the student, who is poor in knowledge, and the תככים is a teacher in the middle, who knows enough to teach but still needs to grow. If the teacher teaches, both gain. If he refuses, a second פסוק shows that ה׳ can switch them, making the teacher foolish and the student wise. The closing words tell us that this whole תורה-based approach belongs to רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person (here, poor in knowledge)
Here read as a person 'in the middle', a teacher who knows some but not all

phrases.english: In a similar way, you say:
"The poor man and the man in the middle meet;
phrases.notes: משלי 29:13. Here תככים is read as someone in the middle: he knows enough to teach, but he still has more to learn.

phrases.english: ה׳ lights up the eyes of both of them."
When the student goes to his teacher
and says to him: "Teach me Torah,"
if he teaches him, then "ה׳ lights up the eyes of both of them."
But if not, then "The rich and the poor meet;
phrases.notes: משלי 22:2

phrases.english: ה׳ is the maker of them all."

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ חָכָם לָזֶה — עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ טִיפֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: The One Who made this one wise now makes him foolish,
and the one He made foolish, He now makes wise.
This is the teaching of Rabbi Natan.

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי נתן's view, a teacher who teaches grows along with his student, and a teacher who refuses can lose his wisdom to that student.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related lesson about תורה learning to the תורה-centered reading of יעבץ's prayer, then names רבי נתן as its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher who teaches a student gains along with him. One who refuses risks having ה׳ make him foolish and the student wise.

steps.title: A second reading of יעבץ's prayer as requests for worldly blessings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא explains each phrase of יעבץ's prayer differently: as requests for children, success in business, good health, and protection from the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא says: 'If You will bless me' means with having children. 'And enlarge my border' means with sons and daughters. 'And let Your hand be with me' means in business. 'And keep me from harm' means that I should not suffer from headaches, earaches, or eye pain. 'So that it will not pain me' means that the יצר הרע should not overpower me and keep me from learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different explanation of the same prayer of יעבץ. This one comes from רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן read every phrase as a request about תורה. רבי יהודה הנשיא reads most of them as requests about everyday life: family, income, and health. Only the last phrase, about the יצר הרע keeping him from learning, still connects to תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
"If You will bless me" means with having children;
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 4:10, the same prayer of יעבץ, now explained differently.

phrases.english: "And enlarge my border" means with sons and daughters;
"And let Your hand be with me" means in business;
"And keep me from harm" means
that I should not have a headache
or an earache or eye pain;
"So that it will not pain me" means
that the evil inclination should not overpower me and keep me from learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, mostly worldly reading of the same prayer that רבי נתן read as being about תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעבץ asked for children, success in business, good health, and protection from the יצר הרע so he could keep learning.

steps.title: יעבץ's plea and God's answer in רבי יהודה הנשיא's reading
steps.stepSummary: יעבץ says that if God grants these things, good. If not, he will go to the grave in sadness. God gives him what he asked for.
steps.simpleTranslation: If You do this, good. And if not, I will go down to the grave in sadness. 'And God brought him what he asked for.'
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי יהודה הנשיא's version of the prayer. It ends the same way as the first version: יעבץ's plea, and then God answers him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings end with the same words from the פסוק, 'God brought him what he asked for.' This proves again the point from step 22, that God answered עתניאל, who is the same person as יעבץ. The two sages disagree only about what he asked for.

keyTerms.meaning: The grave; the place of the dead

phrases.english: If You do this, good;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — הֲרֵינִי הוֹלֵךְ בִּנְסִיסִי לַשְּׁאוֹל,
phrases.english: and if not, I will go down sad to the grave.
"And God brought him what he asked for."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 4:10

steps.whatToRemember: Both sages agree that God answered יעבץ's prayer. They argue only about what the prayer asked for: תורה (רבי נתן) or mostly worldly blessings (רבי יהודה הנשיא).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי יהודה הנשיא's reading with the same ending as step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: God granted יעבץ's request, which again answers the question from step 22.

steps.title: The same פסוק applied to a poor person asking a rich man for help
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in משלי is now applied to money. If a homeowner supports a poor person, good. If not, ה׳ can make the rich man poor and the poor man rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, you can explain: 'The poor man and the man of means meet; ה׳ lights up the eyes of both of them.' When a poor person goes to a homeowner and says 'Support me,' if he supports him, good. If not, 'the rich and the poor meet; ה׳ made them all': the One Who made this one rich can make him poor, and the One Who made that one poor can make him rich.
steps.whatsHappening: This matches רבי יהודה הנשיא's worldly reading. The גמרא applies the same פסוק to a case about money instead of תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 26 exactly, but with wealth in place of wisdom. A rich man who refuses to give charity can lose his wealth to the poor man he turned away. The two pairs of steps line up: רבי נתן's תורה reading matches the teacher case, and רבי יהודה הנשיא's worldly reading matches the charity case.

keyTerms.meaning: A homeowner; here, a person with money

phrases.english: In a similar way, you say:
"The poor man and the man of means meet;
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before (משלי 29:13), but now it is about money instead of תורה.

phrases.english: ה׳ lights up the eyes of both of them."

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעָנִי הוֹלֵךְ אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: When a poor person goes to a homeowner
and says: "Support me,"
if he supports him, good;
but if not, then "The rich and the poor meet;
ה׳ is the maker of them all."

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ עָשִׁיר לָזֶה — עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ עָנִי,
phrases.english: The One Who made this one rich now makes him poor,
and the one He made poor, He now makes rich.

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק teaches two parallel lessons. Whoever refuses to share what ה׳ gave him, whether wisdom or wealth, can have it switched with the person he turned away.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the worldly version of step 26's lesson, matching רבי יהודה הנשיא's worldly reading of the prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rich man who refuses to support a poor person risks having ה׳ make him poor and the poor man rich.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי שמעון's statement
steps.stepSummary: The אגדה is over. The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה so it can start discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: 'Just as we found,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The side story is finished, and the גמרא is going back to the משנה. It quotes only the first words of רבי שמעון's statement, which sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון says that some rules for a חטאת apply only to a private person's חטאת and not to a communal one. Just as this is true of the child of a חטאת, its substitute, and one whose owner died, it is also true of a חטאת whose owner already got atonement and one that is over a year old. The word כו׳ means the full quote is assumed, so the learner should look back at the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as we found; a comparison to a known case
Etc.; the rest of the quote is assumed
A חטאת brought by one person
A חטאת brought for the whole community

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement of רבי שמעון. It only quotes the משנה again so the גמרא can begin explaining it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
"Just as we found," etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means "and so on." The גמרא quotes just the start of רבי שמעון's line in the משנה and expects you to know the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about יעבץ and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון compares the cases: the rules for a חטאת whose owner already got atonement, or one over a year old, apply to a private חטאת and not to a communal חטאת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's list of five sin offerings that are left to die
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי שמעון listing five kinds of חטאת that are left to die instead of being offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: רבי שמעון says there are five sin offerings that are left to die. They are the baby of a חטאת, an animal swapped for a חטאת, a חטאת whose owner died, a חטאת whose owner already got atonement with another animal, and a חטאת that is past its first year.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after quoting רבי שמעון's words from the משנה, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with his full list of the five חטאות מתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these animals is still holy, but none of them can be offered. So the animal is simply left until it dies. This list sets up the next question: do these rules also apply to offerings that belong to the whole community?

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offerings that are left to die because they can never be offered
The baby born to a female animal set aside as a חטאת
An animal someone tried to swap for a חטאת. It becomes holy too.
Its owner already got atonement, using a different animal
Its year has passed. The animal is now older than one year.

steps.whatToRemember: There are five חטאות מתות: the baby, the swap, the owner died, the owner already got atonement, and the animal is past its year.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
Five sin offerings are left to die,
phrases.notes: Literally "die." They aren't killed. They are kept away until they die on their own.

phrases.english: the offspring of a sin offering, and the substitute of a sin offering,
and a sin offering whose owner died,
and a sin offering whose owner already achieved atonement,
and a sin offering whose year has passed.
phrases.notes: A חטאת has to be in its first year, so once it is older it can't be offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on רבי שמעון's statement from the משנה that was quoted in Step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five kinds of חטאת are never offered and are left to die.

steps.title: Three of the five cases cannot happen with a communal offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון shows that the baby, the swap, and the case where the owner died can never happen with a communal חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can't have the baby of a communal חטאת, because the community never brings a female חטאת. You can't have a swap for a communal חטאת, because the community cannot make a תמורה. You can't have a communal חטאת whose owner died, because the community never dies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון goes through three of his five cases. He shows that each one is impossible when the offering belongs to the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case gets its own reason. Communal sin offerings are always male, so they can't give birth. The community has no power to make a תמורה. And a community as a whole never dies. So these three rules can only ever apply to an individual's offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The community. A communal offering belongs to all of כלל ישראל.
A female sin offering. The community never brings one.
A community cannot make a substitute for its offering

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר וְלַד חַטָּאת בְּצִיבּוּר —
phrases.english: You cannot say there is an offspring of a sin offering in the community —
because there is no female sin offering in the community,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר תְּמוּרַת חַטָּאת בְּצִיבּוּר —
phrases.english: and you cannot say there is a substitute of a sin offering in the community —
because a community does not make a substitute,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר חַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ בְּצִיבּוּר —
phrases.english: and you cannot say there is a sin offering whose owners died in the community —
because the community does not die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר וְלַד חַטָּאת בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the list from Step 31 and shows that three of its items can only apply to an individual.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baby, the swap, and the owner-died cases apply only to an individual's חטאת.

steps.title: What about the last two cases?
steps.stepSummary: For the case where the owner already got atonement and the case where the animal is past its year, nothing says clearly that they don't apply to the community. So maybe they apply to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for a חטאת whose owners already got atonement, or one whose year passed, we haven't found a reason like that. So maybe these two rules apply both to an individual and to the community?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question. These two cases could happen with a communal offering, so maybe they apply there too. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A community can set aside an extra animal and get atonement with another one, and a communal animal can grow older than a year. So the simple reasons from Step 32 don't work here. That opens the possibility that these two rules also cover the ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: We have not found a clear source or reason
An individual person, as opposed to the community
They are in effect, they apply

phrases.english: One whose owners achieved atonement, and one whose year passed —
we have not found that these can't happen with the community.
One might think they should apply
both to an individual and to the community?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מָצִינוּ. יָכוֹל יְהוּ נוֹהֲגוֹת בֵּין בְּיָחִיד בֵּין בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the reasons in Step 32 don't cover the remaining two cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the rules for a חטאת whose owner already got atonement, and a חטאת past its year, also apply to communal offerings?

steps.title: Learn the unclear cases from the clear ones
steps.stepSummary: Using the rule of learning the unclear from the clear, all five rules apply only to an individual's offering, not to the community's.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say that a person learns the unclear from the clear. The clear cases apply only to an individual and not to the community. So the cases where the owner already got atonement, or the animal is past its year, also apply only to an individual and not to the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The two unclear cases are treated like the three clear ones, so they apply only to an individual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five cases come together as one group. Three of them clearly apply only to an individual. So we assume the whole group works the same way, and the remaining two also apply only to an individual. In the end, a communal חטאת is never left to die because of these rules.

keyTerms.meaning: A person learns the unclear case from the clear case
These things are said, meaning the rule applies to this case

steps.whatToRemember: All five חטאות מתות apply only to an individual's offering. Three can't happen with the community at all, and the other two are learned from those three.
steps.confusionAlert: The last two cases could happen with a communal animal. The rule still doesn't apply to the community, because we learn these cases from the clear ones.

phrases.english: You must say: a person learns the unspecified from the specified,
just as the specified cases apply to an individual and not to the community,
phrases.notes: The "specified" cases are the three from Step 32: the baby, the swap, and the owner who died.

phrases.english: so too, with one whose owners achieved atonement and one whose year passed,
these things are said about an individual and not about the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 33 by comparing the unclear cases to the clear ones from Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two unclear cases follow the three clear ones, so they apply only to an individual and not to the community.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All five חטאות מתות apply only to an individual's offering, never to a communal one.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a basic method: when items in a group are listed together, the clear ones show us how to understand the unclear ones.
